## Description

This vignette reports the results of a longer perturbation analyses (*not* that ran in the previous vignette). This was built on the same vital rate models as in [Single VR Model](DIPM-020_Vital_rate_models.html), but where the IPM was run with limits from -200 to +200, with increments of 0.2 m (`n. bins = 2000`), and for 12 months. This perturbation is time consuming (~ 4h) to be rendered as a vignette efficiently. I will here load the results of the perturbation analyses stored in the folder `results_tokeep`.

## Setup

Loading data, packages, and models.

```{r}
# packages
library(whereipm)
library(tidyverse)


# IPM models
phasesIPMs <- readRDS(file.path(here::here(), "results_tokeep", "K2000x12_20190330",
                                "phaseModelsIPMs_K2000x12.rds"))
perturbationResults <- readRDS(file.path(here::here(), "results_tokeep", "K2000x12_20190330",
                                         "perturbation_result_phase_models_K2000x12.rds"))
# extracting output list
outputs <- rownames(perturbationResults)

# colors
Cols <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Darjeeling1", 3, type = "discrete")
```

## Plotting

### IPM results

```{r}
# Early phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour", 
                colorscale = 'Jet')
# Mid phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour", 
                colorscale = 'Jet')
# Late phase
plotly::plot_ly(x=1:ncol(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$pop.size), 
                y=rev(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$kernel.params$y), 
                z=phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]]$pop.size, 
                type="contour", 
                colorscale = 'Jet')


quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[1]], "Init")
quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[2]], "Middle")
quick.plot(phasesIPMs$IPMs[[3]], "End")
```

### Comparing output variables

I am here plotting the output variables from the three IPMs.

```{r, fig.height = 15}
# obtaining the original values for output variables:
phasesIPMs <- phasesIPMs %>%
  mutate(
    orig.output =   map(IPMs, function(x){
      outs <- lapply(outputs, function(i){x[[i]]})
      names(outs) = outputs
      return(outs)
      }
      ))

# extracting original parameters and reading them for plotting
orig_outputs <- phasesIPMs %>%
  select(orig.output) %>%
  pull() %>%
  unlist() %>%
  matrix(ncol = nrow(phasesIPMs), nrow = length(outputs)) %>%
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame()
colnames(orig_outputs) <- outputs
rownames(orig_outputs) <- unlist(phasesIPMs$phase)

# checking
orig_outputs

# looping the plot
par(mfrow = c(round(length(outputs)/2), 2))
for(i in 1:dim(orig_outputs)[2]){
  plot(orig_outputs[[i]], type='l', main = colnames(orig_outputs)[i], xlim = c(0.7, 3.3),
     xaxt = 'n', ylab = '', xlab = '', las = 1)
  axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = c('Initial', 'Middle', 'End'), las=1)
  points(orig_outputs[[i]], col = Cols, pch=19, cex = 1.5)
  text(1:3 + 0.1, orig_outputs[[i]], 
     labels = round(as.numeric(orig_outputs[[i]]), 2), cex = 1)
}
```

### Plotting perturbation results

Here, I am not running the perturbation analyses (too time consuming), but rather loading a stored perturbation result.

First, loading the perturbation results and rearranging the format to make it easier to plot.

**NOTE**: reproduction probability is here to be interpreted as the opposite of it. It is coded as the probability to *not* reproduce. So what appears to be a negative effect is actually a positive effect on the probability to have any offspring.

```{r}
# For ease of plotting, handling the array t make it a single data.frame with outputs for columns and parameters for rows

pResults <- aperm(perturbationResults, perm = c(2,1,3))
pResults <- data.frame(apply(pResults, 2, c),
                       expand.grid(dimnames(perturbationResults)[c(2,3)]))
colnames(pResults)[(ncol(pResults)-1):ncol(pResults)] <- c("params", "phase")

# creating a vector of better names for parameteres
paramnames <- c('survival (int)', 'survival (slo)',
            'repr p (int)',  'repr p (slo)',
            'offspr n (int)',  'offspr n (slo)',
            'ad dispersal (int)','ad dispersal (slo)',
            'ad distance (mean)', 'ad distance (sd)',
            'nat dispersal (int)','nat dispersal (slo)',
            'nat dispersal (landsc)', 'nat dispersal (loc x land)',
            'nat distance (mean)', 'nat distance (sd)')

## plotting all outputs
for(i in outputs){
  p <- ggplot(data = pResults, aes_string(x = "params", y = i, fill = "phase")) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", width = 0.8, position = position_dodge()) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = Cols) +
    coord_flip()
  theme_minimal()
print(p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0)) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = paramnames) +
  ggtitle(as.character(i)))
}
```
